_comment: WP8.1 Store interception lab. Everything the server does is driven by this file.

network._comment_advertiseIp: 'auto' picks the LAN IPv4 of the default route; override with an explicit address when the PC has several NICs.

dns._comment_bind: 'auto' tries the LAN address first, then 0.0.0.0. Needed because Windows ICS parks on 0.0.0.0:53.

hijack._comment: Names matching these globs resolve to advertiseIp instead of the real address. Start narrow: only what the capture proves is Store traffic.
hijack._comment_hosts: The marketplace image/content hosts come from Microsoft partners' own firewall guidance for Windows 8.1 store access, which names them alongside marketplaceedgeservice.
hijack._comment_account: The account group that used to be listed here is GONE as of 2026-10-15 22:00 local, because the cost the earlier comment named turned out to be the point: login.live.com, clientconfig.passport.net and go.microsoft.com are alive on the real network, and this lab was answering them 502, so every attempt the Store made on its own account and configuration path ended in a failure this lab injected. account.nokia.com and az717532.vo.msecnd.net are gone for the same reason even though they are dead on the real network: hijacking a dead name only changes which failure the device gets, and it was answering a Nokia account service four times with 502. The question changed - the lab is no longer reading what the device asks, it is trying to serve a page that renders - and dns.logQueries still records every query, hijacked or not, so nothing that was being watched is now unseen. ssl-api.bing.com stays, for the reason E-003 gave: it answers nothing on the real network either, so it is not an injected failure. Undo: the five names are written out in docs/FINDINGS.md E-004.

proxy._comment_tls: Direct TLS listener on 443: a device redirected by DNS alone connects here without needing any proxy setting.
proxy._comment_http: Plain-HTTP listener on 80: the 8.1 store lookups, search and app images are served over HTTP, so without this the device resolves the hijacked name, connects to 80 and only gets a RST.

mitm._comment: Only these hosts are TLS-intercepted. Every other host is tunnelled byte-for-byte and never decrypted, so unrelated device traffic is untouched.
mitm._comment_account: The diagnostic group that used to end this list is gone from both lists at once, because a name hijacked in one and not the other is a name whose traffic is a tunnel - see dns.hijack._comment_account for why the five account names were removed and why ssl-api.bing.com stays.

upstream._comment: insecure=false keeps certificate validation on when we relay to the real backend.

livestore._comment: Zinc API (Live Store Public API). Get a key from the One Live Developer Centre, app for the Live Store realm.
livestore._comment_protocol: Answers the Store endpoints the phone itself calls (the storePages home page, the hub pages, the application lists) with the Zune catalog XML it reads. The backend behind those names is gone - the CDN answers 503 and the other hosts do not resolve - so the page has to be served, not relayed.

protocol._comment: catalogFile is read relative to this folder and re-read when it changes, so dropping in a real catalog does not need a restart. demo-catalog.json is a fake store of invented apps - enough sections to see what the page renders; every entry is invented and every publisher says Lab Fixture. sample-catalog.json is the three-entry fixture the tests use as a baseline.
protocol._comment_hubTemplate: The layout the page asks the client to render it with, read from the phone rather than guessed. The phone's own Store UI names this style: ZuneAssets480x800.dll carries Store_DynamicHubStyle_TitleMargins, Store_DynamicHubStyle_TitleStyle_FontSize and Store_DynamicHubStyle_VScrollContentMargins. See src/store/vocabulary.mjs for the offsets.
protocol._comment_templateType: The template type a store page is rendered with, and it is a NUMBER, not a name: the phone's UI assets style exactly Store_Hub_TemplateType003, 004, 015 and 017 for a hub page, and Store_Chart_TemplateType010 for a chart. 003 is the plain ordered list, which is what a generated section is. A name here - 'DynamicHub', or the 'GamesHub' of the archived page - is a token this phone cannot style.
protocol._comment_templateTypeForm: Whether the type key travels as an attribute of <Template> or as a child element. The parser holds it as a property name, not as markup, so nothing on the phone decides it; 'both' writes it either way. One of: attribute, element, both.
protocol._comment_pageFormat: The document the page endpoint answers with. 'storePage' is the grammar the phone's own parser describes: a StorePage root carrying Panes, Templates and the entries, where a pane names its section and the items are in the feed underneath. 'panes' is that same document with each pane ALSO carrying its own editorialItems and applications - the arrangement of the archived response, where the entry a pane points at holds its items inline, so the client is never asked to resolve a reference to content it has already been sent. 'atom' is the older <a:feed> shape that archived responses and the app-detail feeds use. Every page the lab served before 'storePage' was 'atom', and the phone asserted on all of them. One of: storePage, panes, atom. Currently 'panes': that variant is armed for a run, because it is the one arrangement the phone has not been shown - it has met 'storePage' many times and asserted on it every time. Set it back to 'storePage' and POST /__lab/reload to un-arm it.
protocol._comment_appList: The entry shape of the application list, taken from the archived responses of the real service rather than from this lab's own earlier feed. Both archived generations of the endpoint - /v9/catalog/apps (2016-05-06) and /v8/catalog/apps (2013-12-16), saved byte for byte in src/store/fixtures/archive/real-apps-feed-*.xml - carry `<k>` on every entry, immediately after `impressionId`; neither carries the bare `<title>` this lab wrote on each entry, because an app's name travels as `a:title` plus `sortTitle` and the only `<title>` at entry level is the one inside a `category`. READING THE OLDER OF THE TWO IS WHAT SHRANK THIS CHANGE: v8 also carries `<mediaInstanceId>` in every offer, `WindowsPhone80` beside `WindowsPhone81` in clientTypes, and `<a:link rel="next">` with `<pagingToken>` at feed level - and the v9 capture of the same endpoint carries none of those, so they are properties of the older generation's service and not of the entry shape, and nothing here writes them. The one element that survives both generations is `<k>`, which is why it is the one being added. Both captures put 4 on the first entry and +1 each (to 17 over 14 entries, to 53 over 50) - the offset of 3 is observed and not explained, so it is a configurable seed and not a constant. `appListRank` is '' for no `<k>` at all (every feed this lab served before the archive was read); `appListEntryTitle` true restores the bare `<title>`. Undo: set appListRank back to "" and appListEntryTitle back to true, then POST /__lab/reload - nothing but config moves, and neither value is read by the page endpoint.
protocol._comment_pageCookie: A page cookie, armed as an experiment on 2026-10-15 22:20 local. `X-WP-StorePage-Cookie` is the ONLY header the client reads back from a response (`WPSHeaderHandler::GetStorePageCookie`, @47028, reading the name at @46984), it keeps the value in the registry (`WPSStorePageCookie`, @41876), and it adds it to its own requests (`::AddStorePageCookie`, @46944). This lab has never sent one, which is why no request from the device carries it. Empty means off. The value is a 32-hex token because the protocol spells its own ids that way; what the client does with it is unknown beyond store-and-echo, so the reading that matters is whether the next device request carries the header back - which is visible in the capture with nobody watching the screen. Undo: set it back to "".
protocol._comment_dataSource: A pane's data source, armed 2026-10-15 23:40 local. The phone's own parser says a pane is not a container that holds items but a pointer: `PANE_FIELDS` in src/store/vocabulary.mjs holds /DataSource/Type and /DataSource/Url (@14112, @14148, both read out of H:\Windows\System32\ZMarketplace.dll), `ProcessEntryFromType` creates its objects from a FeedType and a Url together ('Create StoreObjects with FeedType = %S Url = %S ', @28920), and the download that follows has its own function names in the binary (PendingListDownload::ParseFromStream, ::OnDownloadAvailable, ::OnRequestFailed, @27772, @118552, @118596). Every page this lab has served has had panes with no source, which is a pane the client cannot fetch content for - and F-005's one-request cycle is what that looks like from the outside. The URL written is absolute, on the host the device reached this lab through, so the download the client triggers comes back here and is visible in the capture without anyone watching the screen; F-019 makes a download the first self-observing sign of a page that parsed. Undo: set it back to false.
protocol._comment_dataSourceType: Which feed type each pane's source announces: one of the four the client has a parser for (Applications, FeaturedApps, Collections, Categories - see DATA_SOURCE_TYPES in vocabulary.mjs). 'Applications' is the one whose parser matches what /v9/catalog/apps answers with, an ordered list of application entries, so it is the only one this lab can serve today. An unknown value falls back to it rather than writing a type the client cannot read.
protocol._comment_paneType: What a pane says it *is*. Armed 2026-10-16 05:20 UTC with `inv` (a token from the page parser's literal pool, result negative) and re-armed 2026-10-16 07:25 UTC with `Collection` (a page-family token - negative over every document served since). It is back on `Collection` because the reading that briefly moved it to `Applications` on 2026-10-20 does not survive the property map: the pane's own map carries `/Type` as its OWN field (@319-324 in the map at 0x10004ca4-0x10004d58 of the carved ZMarketplace.dll), and the feed type and URL are a different pair, `/DataSource/Type` (prop 326) and `/DataSource/Url` (prop 327), both of which this lab already writes as `Applications` plus the section URL. So `<Type>` is not where `Create StoreObjects with FeedType = %S Url = %S` takes its first argument from, and changing it was a guess dressed as a reading - reverted the same day (F-036). What is still unknown is the VALUE this field may carry; `Collection` is the only one with a pool token beside it. Undo: nothing to undo - this is the value every delivery since 2026-10-16 carried.
protocol._comment_panesInFeed: Where the panes sit in the page document, armed 2026-10-20 as the next single variable after F-036. `/Panes/Pane` is an absolute path in the parser, and this document has two roots it could be read from: `<StorePage>` (every delivery so far) and the `<a:feed>` nested inside it (never served). The parser's own parser selects the feed for the entries (`/feed/entry`), so a walk that reads the pane path from the feed node would find panes only in `<StorePage><a:feed><Panes>` - which no page this lab has served has ever carried. READ 2026-10-20 08:30 local, and it turns against the change: `npm run page:diff` reports `/Panes/Pane` and `/Templates/Template` MISSING once the panes travel inside the feed, because both paths are absolute from the document element - and the app list is the proof that an unprefixed path resolves against the catalog namespace, where our panes already are. The flag stays in the code as the tool for the other reading; it is DISARMED. The change moves `<Panes>` and `<Templates>` inside the feed and nothing else: same bytes, same order, same template block, same entries, same pane fields. The response header x-lab-pane-placement says feed or page, so no capture can be read as the wrong arm. Undo: false + POST /__lab/reload.
protocol._comment_paneSubType: The pane's sub type, the second of the two type fields its property map holds. Nothing read so far says what a value would look like, so it is empty and the page carries no <SubType> at all - a value invented here would be a second variable in the same run.
protocol._comment_paneBackgroundImage: Each pane's own background art, `/BackgroundImage/id`, armed as the next single variable after F-032. Of the four paths in PANE_FIELDS the served pane does not carry - /SubType, /BackgroundImage/id, /LiveTileUpdateInterval, /StoreObjectsForLiveTile - this is the one a hub tile would draw with, and the image endpoint now answers for any guid this lab mints, so arming it changes the page and nothing else. The guid is derived from the section title (`background:<title>`), so it is stable and distinct per pane and recognisable in a capture as this lab's own. What the screen answers: if the page draws, art was required and the frame was otherwise complete; if it stays on the spinner, that hypothesis is out and the count in PANE_FIELDS drops to three. The response header x-lab-pane-background says whether a delivery carried it (guid / none), so no capture can be read as the wrong arm. Off by default; undo: false + POST /__lab/reload.
protocol._comment_offerMediaInstance: Every offer carries `<mediaInstanceId>` right after `<offerId>`, armed 2026-10-17 evening as the single variable for the install failure. Why: the archived response of the real service spells it that way in every offer (real-hub-page-20130813.xml), this lab has never written it because the v9 *application list* capture carries none (F-022), and the client logs the pair it works with when it handles an offer - `wszLicenseType '%S' wszMediaInstanceId '%S'` (F-017). On 2026-10-17 an install attempt from the rendered app list answered `0x80070057` (E_INVALIDARG) with no request leaving the phone (F-033): an install built from an offer that has a licence type and no media instance is the shape that would throw that. The guid is derived from the app (`media:<app id>`), so it is stable and distinct per app. THIS IS A HYPOTHESIS, not a finding - the reading is the next tap: if E_INVALIDARG turns into a request, this was it and the capture will show which host the install asks for; if it stays, the field is not the cause and the next candidate is the offer's `paymentTypes`/`store` pair. It changes application records on every surface (list, detail, page), which is one field in one place. SECOND READING, 2026-10-20, and it turns against the field: with it on, the list of 17 apps asked for NO image at all - zero image requests, and one DNS query for the image host in the whole day, the detail's - where the same list URL on 10-17 (field absent) was followed within a second by 240 icon_small requests for all 17 of the same guids. The two bodies differ only by timestamp, impressionId and this element. So the field is now suspected of costing the list its art, the mechanism is unproven, and it is DISARMED to read that (F-035). Undo and re-arm: set true and POST /__lab/reload - measured that a reload is enough, the flag is read per request, so the 'restart' in the first sentence of this comment was wrong.
protocol._comment_serve: 'generated' builds the page from the catalog. 'archive' serves a response of the real service byte for byte instead. It is NOT a one-variable change, and the header x-lab-archive-warning says why: that archived response is the games hub page of a different client generation, so it carries a template (GamesHub) and a page type this Store client does not own. 'control-broken' serves controlFile instead: a body truncated mid-element on purpose, with the page's own content-type and a correct content-length, so that the only thing that differs from a normal delivery is whether the document can be parsed at all. That is the one variable no page experiment has ever moved - six documents, all plausible, none broken - and the two answers are read differently: same behaviour as a normal page means the client never reaches a parser, different behaviour means it does. The handler refuses with 502 control_unavailable if the file ever ends with a closing bracket, because a repaired fixture is not a control. Undo: put 'generated' back.
protocol._comment_serveE008: E-008 was armed 2026-10-17 15:01 local and answered with one Store open: the truncated body drew error 0xc00cee23 on the handset at 13:02:01Z, where the same request with the built page had drawn silence. The client reaches a parser, so the failure of the built page is inside the document and not before it (F-027). Back to 'generated' the same minute - the control is not a thing to leave armed.
protocol._comment_serveE010: E-010 step 3 was armed 2026-10-17 15:16 local and read at 15:17: the archived real document (29 238 bytes, GamesHub) was delivered to the handset, drew no follow-up request and drew error 88675309 on screen - where six generated pages drew silence. A document from a different generation is rejected as a page; ours is accepted and yields nothing. Back to 'generated' the same minute. Undo: back to 'generated' + POST /__lab/reload.
protocol._comment_mutant: E-010's probe, built 2026-10-17 15:19 local and armed one name at a time. 'serve: mutant' answers the page endpoints with the page the client already accepts, carrying exactly ONE renamed construct; an error on screen means the client reads that construct, silence means it does not - which is the difference six content experiments could not see. Names: root-renamed, panes-renamed, pane-renamed, templates-renamed, template-renamed, datasource-renamed, entries-renamed (PAGE_MUTATIONS in src/store/protocol.mjs). A name that does not exist, or whose element is not in the document, is refused with 502 rather than served as an ordinary page. Undo: empty mutant + serve 'generated' + POST /__lab/reload.
protocol._comment_archiveFile: Points at the derived document armed 2026-10-17 15:2x local: the real 2013 response byte for byte except its template block, which is replaced with the numeric TEMPLATETYPE 003 this phone's UI assets style (the block reads <Templates><Template TEMPLATETYPE="003">...<TEMPLATETYPE>003</TEMPLATETYPE></Template></Templates>). One variable against the 29 238-byte original, which drew 88675309: if the error is the client failing to find a template it can style, this document answers differently. The original is untouched and is one value away. Undo: put the original path back.
protocol._comment_configuration: The configuration endpoint, armed 2026-10-17. `GET /v8/Configuration/Stores/OEMStores/NOKIA` and `/MOStores/` are the two requests this phone makes before it asks for a page, and they have never been answered: the host is hijacked, no handler matched them, so the relay resolved the name back to this process and returned `502 upstream_loop`. On 2026-10-16 at 06:20 UTC the device made eight of them in 735 ms, four tries per store, gave up, and never asked for the page at all in that session - so this is the one request on the client's critical path that the lab drops, and the only one that can fail before the page exists. The document served is a REPLY and not a reconstruction: no capture of this endpoint exists in the archive (F-021) or on the phone (F-020), so the response carries `x-lab-invented: 1` - and since 2026-10-17 that header claims only the VALUES, not the markup. F-024 found the client's own configuration grammar offline in an FFU: a `ConfigurationFile` document with `Domains`/`Domain`/`setting`, where every `{WPAppsMarketplace*}` base is a `<setting>` and the store ids the client lacks (`OEMStoreID`, `MOStoreID`) are settings too. The builder writes that grammar now. What is still inferred is the pairing of that grammar to these two endpoints, because the device's own file carries no store setting at all and these are the two places the client asks at start-up. Measure it by the device's next request: a page fetch that no longer follows a 502, fewer than four retries, or an image request. Undo: set enabled back to false - the route stops matching and the request falls through to passthrough exactly as before.

livestore._comment_provisioning: The device certificate request, armed only for measurement. Why it is here: `devicecertificateservice.windowsphone.com` has been treated as Store traffic by `tools/analyze-captures.mjs` for as long as that tool has had a host list, and no handler has ever answered it - so every such request was a 502 this lab injected, the same defect F-031 found on the image CDN. Why it is shaped this way: no capture of this request exists on the phone, in the archive or in the FFU, so the protocol comes from another project reversing the same era of handsets (ReLiveWP, `POST /dcs/certificaterequest`: `application/pkcs10`, the three `X-Windows-Phone-*` headers, base64 in and base64 PKCS#7 out, `application/c-x509-ca-cert`). That is WP7's contract, not this 8.1 handset's, which is why every answer carries `x-lab-invented: 1` and `x-lab-refused` on the refusals. What it does not do: it does not provision anything the client is known to need, and no capture yet shows the phone asking for this path. Reading it is therefore the same as reading any other armed single variable - the next device request that names this host, or none. Issued chains use a fixed client profile (clientAuth, CA:FALSE, no SAN, no `-copy_extensions`), so a request cannot mint a certificate for another host. Arming it takes three touchpoints on purpose: `enabled` here, the host in `proxy.mitm.hosts`, and the host in `dns.hijack.names`. Undo: enabled false and the host out of both lists. See F-034.
livestore._comment_client: The JSON API of the second client on the handset - the Live Store app, not the system Store. Served by the `store-live-client` handler (src/store/live-client.mjs). Found on 2026-10-17 in that app's own cache (F-029): `store-api.live.net.co` with /apps, /games, /apps/search?q=, /games/search?q=, /app/{id}, /game/{id}, and an account record at /me behind a sign-in at id.live.net.co (client_id=LSS). The field names and value types this handler writes come from those cached responses; the values come from the catalog, which is why every answer carries x-lab-invented: 1. Nothing points at the operator's CDN: icon and r2_url are null, because a URL there would send the handset to a service this lab has no business standing in for. /me answers 401: the lab has no session and will not fabricate an identity. Arming it for the handset takes three touchpoints, on purpose: `enabled: true` here, the host in `proxy.mitm.hosts` (without which the handler refuses with 421 - the router sees every request that reaches the lab, and a bare Host header is not an instruction), and the host in `dns.hijack.names` (without which the handset never comes here at all). That client works today against the real service, so a single value must not be able to take its catalog away. Measured 2026-10-17 on the running lab, after `POST /__lab/reload`: armed, `GET /apps` with the client's Host answers 200, `x-lab-source: live-client`, `x-lab-invented: 1`, `x-lab-count: 17`; disarmed, the same request is passed through to the real service (301) with no lab header. Undo: enabled back to false and the host out of both lists.
livestore._comment_images:
The Store's image CDN, armed 2026-10-17 16:30 local. `cdn.marketplaceimages.windowsphone.com` has been in dns.hijack.names and proxy.mitm.hosts all along, so the lab was answering every icon the handset asked for with its own 502 - 420 of them in two and a half minutes during one search (F-031). Where the real CDN delivered a picture and this lab delivered an error document, the phone's bitmap decode is now handed a real 48x48 PNG instead. What the response says about itself: x-lab-source: store-images, x-lab-image: placeholder, x-lab-invented: 1 - it is not artwork and not any app's icon, and it is the same bytes for every guid and every imagetype. This is a single variable on purpose: the page document is untouched, so if the home page changes, images are the reason; if it does not, they are not. Undo: enabled back to false.
NOTE ON 0x80070057: the handset showed that code on the home page at 14:25-14:26 while these requests were being answered 502. Whether a body that is not a picture is what throws E_INVALIDARG during decode is a HYPOTHESIS this flag tests, not a finding - the page fetch itself answered 200 and 58555 bytes, exactly as it did when it drew silence.
READ AT 16:4x local, one Store open with this armed: the icon slot in the rendered list went from grey to #2E355C, and NO logo is drawn. The first reading of that - 'the client decoded these bytes' - was withdrawn, because a flat field cannot tell our bitmap from the client's own empty-image background: both paint the same square. The placeholder is therefore marked now (a light frame and a diagonal cross on the dark field, x-lab-image-shape says so), and the same open answers the question the colour could not: the mark on screen means the bitmap is drawn, the colour alone means it is not. What that open did settle is the other half - the home page was unchanged, still on the spinner, so the injected 502 was a real defect in every list the client drew and it is not what the page's missing model depends on.
